Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The report is unblocked AfterSell tracker requests (start.aftersell.app/api/public/metrics/log and /api/v1/visibilityEvents) on tommyjohn.com at checkout; the store's AfterSell app embed is loaded, but neither the tracker requests nor the candidate rule could be observed live because the add-to-bag control was refused as a purchase action and both apply_rule phase browsers got a 403 main-document response. The candidate rule ||start.aftersell.app^ (SpywareFilter/sections/tracking_servers.txt) is carried unverified for human review.

## Candidate for review

`||start.aftersell.app^`

SpywareFilter/sections/tracking_servers.txt

Not verified: apply_rule never judged the candidate:⁠ phase A navigation failed (http_blocked) with "main document returned HTTP 403" and the retry failed in phase B with the same HTTP 403, so no phase was captured and the run was told not to retry. The reported requests were also never observed live:⁠ the filtered session's inventory (artifact:⁠har:⁠8e74b4f1-3440-4785-98ad-99e5571396cb) holds no start.aftersell.app request, only the vendor embed cdn.shopify.com/extensions/01a18ee2.../aftersell-utm-triggers.js, because the add-to-bag step could not be rehearsed — the click on #⁠ProductForm-Add was refused with reason "purchase". CLI-route full-page vision reports reporterSymptomPresence indeterminate with no visible instance, as expected for a network-only symptom. Needs a checkout-flow re-test.

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — On www⁠.enago.jp the first-party cookie-consent card still floats over the FAQ content even with the reporter's AdGuard filters active, so I added a domain-scoped element-hiding rule `enago.jp##div[id^="cookie-banner_privacy-trust"]` to the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter; a bounded A/B/C browser experiment confirmed the panel is gone with the page otherwise intact. ## Rule `enago.jp##div[id^="cookie-banner_privacy-trust"]` ## Policy rationale The run instruction's close rules cover first-party advertising, paywalls, German anti-adblock walls, and other anti-adblock walls without a captured detector script; none of them applies to a cookie-consent notice. The repository's filter policy explicitly assigns cookie notices and CMP requests to the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter and states that hiding or blocking the corresponding scripts is sufficient in most cases. The rule is a standard domain-scoped element-hiding `##` rule, which the maintainer rules endorse when hiding alone makes the page work — here the page scrolls normally (html/body overflow visible) and no detector script or gated function is involved. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/b616df6cf6d3b0db87d03b67e81dcb3f9ae7a1aa/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/41270884022 Automated analysis against filters at `b616df6`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.

<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"7f1914805473118e1f12def62e7a5d6364aa9d99c267d7685a243c70ce53383a"} -->
Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — Issue #⁠245937 reports that with AdGuard for Windows enabled the DSM download from the Synology Download Center ends on a browser error page for https:⁠//global.synologydownload.com/...pat (ERR_QUIC_PROTOCOL_ERROR). In the locked AdGuard CLI proxy session the reported page loads cleanly and the baseline blocks only trackers, while no rule in this repository (or in the loaded AdGuard filters) touches the download host; the download itself could not be exercised because the session refuses cross-origin click/navigation and in-page requests, so no filter rule can be shown to cause or fix it.

## Missing information

- No route to exercise the reported cross-origin download request: The reported symptom happens only after the download link is used:⁠ the anchor on www⁠.synology.com points to https:⁠//global.synologydownload.com/download/DSM/release/7.4.1/90080/DSM_DS119j_90080.pat?..., and the reporter's error page shows that URL. In the locked adguard_cli session (issue origin www⁠.synology.com) the anchor click is refused by interact_page with `external_destination`, open_page to the same URL is refused with `navigation_off_origin` ('URL must remain on configured issue origin'), and evaluate_js refuses any fetch()/request. Nothing in the run instruction or repository guidance says how to verify a symptom behind a cross-origin navigation or download that the session cannot perform, so the reported defect can be neither reproduced nor shown absent here.

## Artifacts

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — On www⁠.yepas.com the reported cookie banner is already covered by the existing rule yepas.com#⁠#⁠#⁠cerezizin (applied in the baseline phase), while the third-party Connexease support-chat widget (fixed div.tusla-livechat with a 60x60 launcher at bottom-right) was still shown; the domain-scoped element-hiding rule yepas.com#⁠#⁠.tusla-livechat verified as removing it with page integrity intact and no remaining instances. ## Rule `yepas.com##.tusla-livechat` ## Policy rationale The report is an annoyance (cookie notice + chat widget), not the site's own advertising, a paywall, a German anti-adblock wall, or a non-anti-adblock scam/phishing page, so no policy rule closes it. The chat widget matches the AdGuard Widgets filter purpose:⁠ a chat widget not integrated with the page content and not the main content. The reported cookie banner is already served by the existing rule yepas.com#⁠#⁠#⁠cerezizin, so no duplicate cookie rule is added. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Widgets/sections/widgets.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/41976b8b6c62ab8f708703c639d4d4ee239de629/AnnoyancesFilter/Widgets/sections/widgets.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots

comment.body:

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — onefootball.com still shows its mobile app-install banner ("Get the full live experience with the OneFootball app." + "Get the app") directly under the header, because its CSS-module class no longer matches the existing BannerDownloadTheApp rule. Adding onefootball.com#⁠#⁠div[⁠class*="_bannercontainer"]⁠:⁠has(a[⁠href*="adj.st"]⁠) to the Mobile App Banners filter hides it; the A/B/C experiment on the reported article verified the banner visible before and hidden after with the page intact. ## Rule `onefootball.com##div[class*="_bannercontainer"]:has(a[href*="adj.st"])` ## Policy rationale The report is an annoyance, not one of the report classes the run instruction closes:⁠ it is not first-party advertising, not a paywall, and not an anti-adblock wall (the page shows no ad-blocker detector and the captured requests contain no anti-adblock loader). The reporter-defined target is a mobile app-install promotion banner, the exact category the repository's Mobile App Banners filter (AnnoyancesFilter/MobileApp) exists for, and the repository already carries onefootball.com#⁠#⁠div[⁠class^="BannerDownloadTheApp"]⁠ for this site (AnnoyancesFilter/MobileApp/sections/mobile-app_specific.txt:⁠4693). The Mobile App Banners policy exception for banners 'located in the headers or in the menus' does not apply:⁠ the element is a static full-width block inside main (div.iZppWa_bannercontainer.hiddenOnDesktop, y=55, 90px of a 812px viewport), below the header and above the article card, not inside the header or a menu. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/MobileApp/sections/mobile-app_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/c34860d3ebb82c3f2fe9f6941c3511e17128da82/AnnoyancesFilter/MobileApp/sections/mobile-app_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The mayragna.net article keeps its Luxeritas theme share widget visible — the wide "Copy" copy-link bar under the title/date and a second share bar plus the "Please share this if you liked it!" prompt at the article end — because the only rule acting there (`##a[href^="//twitter.com/intent/tweet?"]`) hides just the tweet links. Adding the domain-scoped rule `mayragna.net##.sns-msg, #sns-tops, #sns-bottoms` was verified in the reporter's own filter profile:⁠ share widget gone, page integrity intact, no remaining instances. ## Rule `mayragna.net##.sns-msg, #sns-tops, #sns-bottoms` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale A social share widget (Like/Share/copy-link buttons) is exactly what the AdGuard Social Media filter is for; no policy rule closes or hands off this report. Not a paywall, not a German anti-adblock wall, not an anti-adblock wall at all — the page shows no detector, gate, scam or dangerous content. The widget is first-party theme markup served in the HTML with no distinct vendor request, so element hiding is the policy-consistent remedy. ## Place in the list [SocialFilter/sections/specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/c34860d3ebb82c3f2fe9f6941c3511e17128da82/SocialFilter/sections/specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/41291964333 Automated analysis against filters at `c34860d`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The "Info küpsiste kohta" cookie-consent dialog on www⁠.apothekabeauty.ee is not handled by the current lists and dims plus scroll-locks the login page. Accepting in a rehearsal set a cookie named gdpr_cookie_token — the same cookie the repository already suppresses for the sister site apotheka.ee — and a domain-scoped set-cookie scriptlet for it was verified to remove the dialog with page integrity intact. ## Rule `apothekabeauty.ee#%#//scriptlet('set-cookie', 'gdpr_cookie_token', '1')` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The report is a cookie notice, which the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter exists to handle; no policy rule closes or hands it off. It is not first-party advertising, not a paywall, and not an anti-adblock wall. The fix extends an existing shared rule of the same platform instead of blocking a page-owned resource, and no traffic or quality criterion of the policy excludes it. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/ff0de93f3d7baf1d98883329f0576a4b847e7293/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — suno.com shows a full-screen app-install modal ("Get the full app experience" with an "Open Suno" button, dimming backdrop and close X) over the mobile page; a domain-scoped element-hiding rule on the portal wrapper that contains that dialog was verified in the filtered baseline, removing the prompt with the page intact. ## Rule `suno.com##div[data-base-ui-portal]:has(div[role="dialog"] img[alt="Suno app"])` ## Policy rationale The report is a website-filtering annoyance, not first-party advertising of the ad-blocking kind:⁠ the filter policy defines the AdGuard Mobile App Banners filter as one that blocks banners and popups encouraging visitors to install mobile apps, and the reporter has that filter enabled - so the fixed modal is in the repository's own documented scope. Not a paywall (the page's composer is shown behind the prompt and needs no purchase) and not an anti-adblock wall (no detector script; get_network_log and get_applied_rules show no anti-adblock mechanism), so no policy exception applies. Traffic/quality bar:⁠ suno.com is a high-traffic site that already carries 13 rules in this repository across five filters, so the added domain-scoped cosmetic rule adds no new risk to the lists. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/MobileApp/sections/mobile-app_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/ff0de93f3d7baf1d98883329f0576a4b847e7293/AnnoyancesFilter/MobileApp/sections/mobile-app_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — On reclaimthenet.org article pages, scrolling injects a full-screen "RECLAIM THE NET" newsletter splash (div.hsp) that also sets html{overflow:⁠hidden}. A single verified CSS-injection rule, `reclaimthenet.org#$#html, .hsp { overflow: visible !important; top: 100000px !important; }`, removes the splash and restores page scrolling. ## Rule `reclaimthenet.org#$#html, .hsp { overflow: visible !important; top: 100000px !important; }` ## Policy rationale Not first-party advertising:⁠ the widget is the site's own newsletter sign-up splash, not an ad for the site's products and not in an ad slot. Not a paywall:⁠ the article content is served and free; the splash only asks for an email and offers 'Maybe later'/'Skip'. Not a German anti-adblock wall and not an anti-adblock wall at all:⁠ the page shows no detector message, and the captured requests contain no detector or anti-adblock script (only first-party Next.js assets). The AdGuard Popups filter's stated purpose covers 'popups and forms for subscribing to news', which is what this splash is, so the repository policy allows a rule here. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/subscriptions_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/ff0de93f3d7baf1d98883329f0576a4b847e7293/AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/subscriptions_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The Äripäev article page keeps a 300px empty ad band above its header (`div.site-hat` holding only an empty `#Panorama_1` slot and a stalled "Reklaam laeb" spinner), with no ad-network request on the page, so the leftover is markup. Hiding it with the domain-scoped rule `aripaev.ee##.site-hat` was verified in the CLI-filtered browser:⁠ band gone, header and article intact, no residue. ## Rule `aripaev.ee##.site-hat` ## Policy rationale The reported defect is a leftover/empty ad container, not the site's own visible first-party advertising, so the 'site's own advertising:⁠ no rule' policy does not apply. No paywall or content-access gate is the subject of the report:⁠ the page's paywall module renders normally and the complaint is the blank ad band above the header. The page shows no anti-adblock wall or detector prompt (no anti-adblock dialog and no detector request in the captured traffic), so the German-wall and other anti-adblock rules do not apply. No other policy criterion (scam/phishing/malware, low traffic, unblocking rules) blocks a domain-scoped cosmetic rule here. ## Place in the list [BaseFilter/sections/foreign.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/ff0de93f3d7baf1d98883329f0576a4b847e7293/BaseFilter/sections/foreign.txt) At the end of the file's regular rules, before [line 14770](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/ff0de93f3d7baf1d98883329f0576a4b847e7293/BaseFilter/sections/foreign.txt#L14770). ## Screenshots

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — proverkacheka.com shows a server-rendered sticky cookie-consent banner («Пользуясь сайтом, вы принимаете политику cookie.» + «Принять») that overlays the receipt form; a domain-scoped cosmetic rule hiding its footer wrapper was verified in the AdGuard CLI proxy baseline (banner gone, page integrity intact). ## Rule `proverkacheka.com##.b-footer_sticky-block` ## Policy rationale The run instruction's filter policy closes German anti-adblock walls, paywalls and the site's own first-party advertising; this report is a plain cookie-consent notice, none of those. It is also not an anti-adblock detector — the page shows no ad-blocker warning and the vision/DOM evidence shows only the cookie notice. The repository's Cookie Notices filter exists for exactly this symptom ('blocks cookie notices on web pages'; 'In most cases, simply hiding or blocking the corresponding scripts is sufficient'), and no CMP request exists to block, so an element-hiding rule is the sanctioned fix. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/ff0de93f3d7baf1d98883329f0576a4b847e7293/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/41308762207 Automated analysis against filters at `ff0de93`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.

<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"9c37accfcb20f9c3a1039c39d4d3b98d9b3b33e015c5904d60bf7c5e1942099c"} -->
Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The reported Italian anti-adblock overlay on www⁠.palermotoday.it ("Hai un adblocker attivo", full-viewport, scroll-locking, produced by the site's inline __unfair detector with captured abacus.jasoncameron.dev detection requests) was reproduced in the locked AdGuard CLI baseline, and the site-scoped element-hiding rule palermotoday.it#⁠#⁠[⁠data-unfair]⁠ hid it in both experiments, but the verdict stayed inconclusive because page integrity could not be confirmed over a pre-existing black video widget; the rule is carried for human review in BaseFilter/sections/antiadblock.txt.

## Candidate for review

`palermotoday.it##[data-unfair]`

BaseFilter/sections/antiadblock.txt

Not verified: Both apply_rule experiments returned environmentExperiment 'inconclusive'. The bound vision review found the reported overlay gone (symptom resolved, remainingInstances empty, adLayoutResidue absent, adElementStatus '[⁠data-unfair]⁠' visible in phase B and hidden in phase C) but left pageIntegrity 'unclear'; its second run also listed a large black media area as observedDamage. Direct DOM evidence shows that black area is the page's own video widget .svp.svp-video-related (375x624, background rgb(0,0,0) at y=1838), present at the same coordinates in the filtered baseline before any candidate rule, so no rule for this report can remove it. The rule was never rejected and no candidate check failed (remainingCandidateAttempts 2); it simply could not be confirmed as verified.

## Missing information

- No way to run the prescribed reporter-profile (settings) validation session in the adguard_cli environment: The run instruction requires that, when the issue carries a reporter import URL, every apply_rule run in a `reported_on_current` session with that import URL (and, when the reporter profile reproduces the symptom, a `defaults_plus_required` comparison). Issue #⁠245958 carries such an import URL, but in the locked adguard_cli environment the launch guidance says to launch every evidence session with extension "none", and that launch refuses `settings` ("A control session (extension \⁠"none\⁠") runs no blocker and takes no \⁠"settings\⁠""). Passing the settings with extension "prepared" instead launched the AdGuard browser extension blocker (pinned release v5.5.2.3, settingsVerified:⁠ false), i.e. a different filtering engine from the locked CLI proxy, without confirming that the import URL was applied. The guidance does not say how to attach a reporter settings import to a CLI-proxy session, so the reporter-profile requirement and the controlled `defaults_plus_required` comparison could not be satisfied; validation was done in extension "none" CLI-proxy sessions whose filterBaseline already mapped the reporter's official filters.

Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — Reproduced the reporter's annotated blank band on russiatoday.ru in the reporter's own filter set, but DOM measurement shows no ad container reserves that space:⁠ every emptied smi2/infox/adfox row is 0x0 with no margin, and the band is the page's own section spacing plus a 30px margin of an emptied comments widget. No element-hiding rule can close it and no ad is served, so this run proposes no rule; process evidence limitation:⁠ no unfiltered reference was obtainable in the adguard_cli environment.

## Missing information

- No unfiltered control route in the adguard_cli environment: The run instruction says to launch every evidence session with extension:⁠"none" because the CLI proxy filters network traffic. In this environment launch_browser refuses `settings` with extension:⁠"none" ("A control session (extension \⁠"none\⁠") runs no blocker and takes no \⁠"settings\⁠"") and requires extension:⁠"prepared" for a session with the reporter's lists. So no truly unfiltered reference page was obtainable, and no filtered-vs-unfiltered comparison of the reported leftover blank space was possible in this run.

`tff-forum.de##.ad-connector`

GermanFilter/sections/specific.txt

comment.body:
<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"642b3edcd75815314782f69ff8d4cfdf9e765ab29a2098deaa3e68d3388fff08"} -->
Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — klmanga.cloud truly shows a first-party anti-adblock wall (「広告ブロッカーを検出しました」) that hides all content and locks scrolling through a per-load randomized class, and it reproduced in both the reporter's own list set and a Base-only session. Three evidence-backed candidates (blocking the TrafficStars/DSP ad stack, preventing the Google ad scripts from loading, allowing gpt.js) all failed to remove it, and no captured request exposes a third-party detector script, so per the repository's anti-adblock policy the report needs a maintainer's look rather than a guessed rule.

## Still visible after the rule

- 今読むべき注目マンガ / カグラバチ / だれでも抱けるキミが好き — Centered anti-adblock wall dialog with the Japanese detection text and blue button is visible over the page. Below and around it, the manga listing area is dark blank/gated, matching the reporter-described whole-page anti-adblock coverage.
- カグラバチ / 社長と酒と星 / 鵺の陰陽師 — At the top edge, the rounded bottom border of the anti-adblock modal/wall remains visible; below it the tile is a dark blank area where the manga listing content is withheld by the anti-adblock state.
- サイコアイズ / だれでも抱けるキミが好き / となりの席のヤツがそういう目で見てくる — Entire supplied tile is a dark blank content region where the manga listings are hidden/gated by the anti-adblock wall; no manga content is visible.
- ゲーム中盤で死ぬ悪役貴族に転生したので、外れスキル【テイム】を駆使して最強を目指してみた / ザ・ファブル The third secret / ケントゥリア — This region is covered by the dark full-page anti-adblock overlay/backdrop; the manga listings identified by the landmark are not visible and the page remains gated by the anti-adblock wall.
- 魔男のイチ / 片田舎のおっさん、剣聖になる / 秘密の授業 — This region is covered by the dark full-page anti-adblock overlay/backdrop; the manga listings identified by the landmark are not visible and the page remains gated by the anti-adblock wall.
- and 3 more of the same, in the run artifacts

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

## Missing information

- No way to read loaded first-party script bodies, so the site's ad-block detection code cannot be identified: The run's tools let me enumerate requests and inspect DOM/CSS, but not to read the source of scripts the page already loaded:⁠ evaluate_js rejects any fetch/XHR, document.scripts only exposes inline text (klmanga.cloud has 6 tiny inline scripts, none referencing the wall), and the wall/detection logic lives in first-party Next.js bundles (/_next/static/chunks/*.js). Without the body of those bundles the detection predicate (which ad element, script or metric the site measures before showing the 「広告ブロッカーを検出しました」 wall) cannot be established, which is exactly the fact the repository policy requires before an anti-adblock rule may be written. A read-only "script source" capability, or HAR response bodies for same-origin scripts, would close this gap.

## Artifacts

https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/41319550627

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — www⁠.lackprofi-plus.de serves its own cookie-consent settings dialog (.ch-cookie-consent, a fixed bottom overlay \~478 px tall) and no list covered it. The same component class is already handled by the shared rule hanse.org,officebase.info,ergonbike.com#⁠#⁠.ch-cookie-consent in the Cookie Notices filter, so the submitted domain-scoped rule extends that rule; it was verified in the current extension build with the dialog gone and page integrity intact. ## Rule `lackprofi-plus.de##.ch-cookie-consent` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The reported problem is a website cookie-consent notice, which is inside the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter's purpose; the instruction's no-rule rules (site's own advertising, paywalls, German anti-adblock walls) do not apply to it. The page shows a consent-settings dialog, not an ad-blocker detection wall asking to disable the blocker, so the anti-adblock gate requiring a captured detector request is not the path taken. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/7cef985195782716dd54b8ab8de7b99d0b5420da/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) By adding the domain to the existing rule on [line 8625](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/7cef985195782716dd54b8ab8de7b99d0b5420da/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt#L8625). ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/41324079444 Automated analysis against filters at `7cef985`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.

The filter policy recommends closing without a rule

## Reproduced symptom

The ads the reporter points at on www⁠.mothergrid.de are the site's own directly-sold advertising:⁠ all creatives and markup are served by mothergrid.de itself through its self-hosted WordPress Advanced Ads plugin, with no ad network or third-party ad server in the request log. Filter policy says the site's own advertising is not deliberately blocked, so this report needs no rule and is recommended for closing.

## Policy rationale

Run instruction, Filter policy:⁠ "The site's own advertising (first-party ads):⁠ no rule; recommend closing." The ad slots the report complains about are served by the site itself, so this rule closes the report before any rule generation. Filter policy document (lookup_rule_guidance, policy topic):⁠ "The site's own advertising should not be deliberately blocked. However, it should not be unblocked if the blocking is caused by general filtering rules" — no blocking rule may be added for these slots, and no unblocking rule is written either. The agent never closes an issue:⁠ this outcome only recommends closing; a maintainer checks and decides.

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The annoyance on www⁠.knowland.hu is the site's own first-party cookie-consent panel (`div#mdCookie`, fixed over the lower half of the mobile article), which no current filter rule hides. A domain-scoped element hiding rule `knowland.hu###mdCookie` was verified in the locked AdGuard CLI baseline:⁠ the panel hides, the article becomes readable, and page layout and content stay intact. ## Rule `knowland.hu###mdCookie` ## Policy rationale The report is a cookie-consent notice annoyance, not one of the closed categories (first-party ads, paywalls, German anti-adblock walls) in the run instruction. The AdGuard Cookie Notices filter policy explicitly allows hiding or blocking the corresponding consent scripts as the usual fix. No anti-adblock wall is involved:⁠ the page shows no detector and the candidate phases recorded antiAdblockDetected:⁠ false. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/ff0de93f3d7baf1d98883329f0576a4b847e7293/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — On www⁠.autozentrum-schmitz.de the site's own German "Cookie Einstellungen" consent modal (#⁠cookie-consent-modal plus its .modal-backdrop) covers the page and, through body.modal-open{overflow:⁠hidden}, locks scrolling, and no rule covers the domain yet. A domain-scoped CSS-injection rule that hides the modal and its backdrop and restores body scrolling was verified in the browser experiment (symptom resolved, page integrity intact, no damage), while plain element hiding was measured to leave the page unscrollable. ## Rule `www.autozentrum-schmitz.de#$#body.modal-open, #cookie-consent-modal.in ~ .modal-backdrop, #cookie-consent-modal { overflow: auto !important; clip: rect(0, 0, 0, 0) !important; }` ## Policy rationale The report is a cookie-notice annoyance:⁠ the page itself shows a German 'Cookie Einstellungen' consent dialog with its backdrop, and the reporter's stated problem is 'cookie'; it is not a German anti-adblock wall, first-party advertising or a paywall, so the run instruction's 'recommend closing' rules do not apply. The Cookie Notices filter's stated purpose covers exactly this:⁠ it blocks cookie notices and CMP requests, hiding or restyling the notice when no consent simulation is needed, which matches a first-party consent dialog with no third-party CMP loader in the captured requests. No existing rule covers www⁠.autozentrum-schmitz.de (domain inventory returned 0 matches), and the closest rules are per-site groups, so a new domain-scoped rule is appropriate. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/7cef985195782716dd54b8ab8de7b99d0b5420da/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/41323875155 Automated analysis against filters at `7cef985`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — ticketfacil.com.br shows a fixed LGPD cookie-consent bar (`div.lgpd-container`, z-index 9999999) over its event listings, as the reporter's screenshot shows, and no enabled list hides it. The repo already has `cuponomia.com.br,madeiramadeira.com.br,lojaasus.com.br##.lgpd-container`, so the fix is adding ticketfacil.com.br to that shared rule; the domain-scoped rule `ticketfacil.com.br##.lgpd-container` verified in the browser extension with the banner gone and the page intact. ## Rule `ticketfacil.com.br##.lgpd-container` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The report is a cookie-consent annoyance (AdGuard Cookie Notices list); it is not the site's own advertising, not a paywall and not a German anti-adblock wall, so none of the run instruction's close rules applies. No anti-adblock gate is involved:⁠ no detector script request was captured and the page carries no 'disable your ad blocker' message. A shared rule for the exact selector already exists, so the maintainer rule to extend shared rules applies and no site-only duplicate is created. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/1a85a19d30ea3d200f291a1a6a328c8836f0fd47/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) By adding the domain to the existing rule on [line 11080](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/1a85a19d30ea3d200f291a1a6a328c8836f0fd47/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt#L11080). ## Screenshots

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The reporter's Assine Abril self-promotion block on vejasp.abril.com.br reappeared because the site renamed its widget class, so the existing rule `abril.com.br##.widget_abril_barra_assine_widget` no longer matches. Adding `vejasp.abril.com.br##.widget_abril_barra_assine_widget_carroussel` to AnnoyancesFilter/Other/sections/self-promo.txt hides the carousel and its benefits block, and the apply_rule experiment verified it with page integrity intact. ## Rule `vejasp.abril.com.br##.widget_abril_barra_assine_widget_carroussel` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The reported element is the publisher's self-promotion widget, which the repository's policy assigns to AdGuard Other Annoyances ('Block self-promotion of websites ... if it is considered an annoying element'), not first-party ad inventory. The repository already keeps a rule for this exact widget family on this domain (abril.com.br#⁠#⁠.widget_abril_barra_assine_widget, AnnoyancesFilter/Other/sections/self-promo.txt:⁠2584); the report asks that the previously working hiding be restored after the site renamed its class, so this is maintenance of an accepted rule family, and the host merges the reported-domain candidate into that shared rule's file. No paywall, anti-adblock, or other closing rule applies:⁠ the page shows no detector wall and no gate; the only reported defect is the visible subscription-promotion block. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Other/sections/self-promo.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/7cef985195782716dd54b8ab8de7b99d0b5420da/AnnoyancesFilter/Other/sections/self-promo.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots

<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"6ae8f163bd6069093e975002d57ed889f318e41659b62bdedd23d767759192f1"} -->
Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The reported annoyance is the site's own Chakra UI "Cookies" consent modal (first-party, no third-party CMP host) which covers the North Cape article and, through its `body[data-scroll-locked]` CSS rule, locks page scrolling. I propose one domain-scoped CSS-injection rule that both moves the modal and its overlay off-screen and restores scrolling, but `apply_rule` could not judge it:⁠ both experiment calls failed in phase A with HTTP 403 on the main document.

## Candidate for review

`visitnorway.com#$#html, .chakra-modal__content-container, .chakra-modal__overlay { overflow: auto !important; top: 100000px !important; }`

AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt

Not verified: apply_rule could not judge this candidate:⁠ both calls failed in phase A with "Phase A navigation failed (http_blocked):⁠ main document returned HTTP 403" (the second call returned retryable=false with finish_fix_analysis_only), so the site refused the phase browser and neither the ordinary `##` element-hiding check that must precede CSS injection nor this injection rule received a visual-review or page-scroll verdict. The rule carries no review verdict and no page-integrity result; the choice of CSS injection over plain `##` rests on live DOM evidence (site stylesheet `body[data-scroll-locked] { overflow: hidden !important; … }` with `data-scroll-locked="1"` on body), not on an experiment.

## Artifacts

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — parisnordkapp.com/the-event shows a first-party "Cookies and privacy" bar fixed over the bottom of the article; a domain-scoped hide of its `.rb-cookie` container was verified to remove it with the page left intact. ## Rule `parisnordkapp.com##.rb-cookie` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale Report is a cookie-notice annoyance, not first-party advertising, a paywall, or an anti-adblock wall, so none of the run instruction's no-rule cases applies. The run instruction and filter policy place cookie-notice fixes in the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter, which permits hiding a notice that overlays content when the page still works. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/388937a7d96b575fb53e95d11b7bc8860d4bccaf/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — Issue #⁠245977 reports two first-party self-promo annoyances on the VK WorkSpace admin billing page (a full-screen divkit promo modal for the VK chatbot and an onboarding tooltip). comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — raspi-tutorials.com shows a full-screen "Subscribe to Blog" newsletter modal (Green Popups/lepopup plugin) over a dark dimming layer after scrolling and waiting, matching the reporter's screenshot. A domain-scoped element-hiding rule for the plugin's popup overlay and popup container was verified in the reporter-profile extension session:⁠ modal and dimmer gone, page intact, scrolling unaffected. ## Rule `raspi-tutorials.com##.lepopup-popup-overlay, .lepopup-popup-container` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The reported element is a newsletter subscription popup, which the AdGuard Popups filter's stated purpose explicitly includes ('Popups and forms for subscribing to news'), so the fix belongs in an Annoyances filter. It is not the site's own advertising, not a paywall, and not an anti-adblock wall, so none of the run instruction's close/hand-off rules applies. No rule of the repository's policy blocks generating this rule; hiding the popup leaves the page fully usable (content unlocked, scrolling works, page integrity intact). ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/subscriptions_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/1a85a19d30ea3d200f291a1a6a328c8836f0fd47/AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/subscriptions_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/41331496126 Automated analysis against filters at `1a85a19`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.

comment.body:
<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"5f36d2db016da5b56f69d072d57f928b6ded36bc645c0db8ab9a4a4f409fd66b"} -->
Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — northcape4000.com really shows an iubenda cookie dialog (loaded by cdn.iubenda.com/cookie_solution/…/core-en.js) that no published rule covers, and adding the domain to the existing shared rule `||cdn.iubenda.com/cookie_solution/$domain=iubenda.com|ebury.com` removes it in testing. Both that network block and a cosmetic hide of `tb-banner-wrapper` were refused by the vision review because the page's own pre-existing "Accept the Privacy to watch the tribute" gate on a consent-suppressed YouTube iframe stays, which no policy-compliant rule can unlock, so a maintainer must decide.

## Still visible after the rule

- Accept the Privacy to watch the tribute (large blank video area) — A privacy-consent gate placeholder reading “Accept the Privacy to watch the tribute” with an info icon appears over a large empty video panel. The tribute video content is withheld behind the consent action, so this is a matching consent-gated placeholder instance; the gated content is not visible.

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

## Missing information

- Policy on consent-gated third-party embeds (CMP notice + gated iframe) is missing: On northcape4000.com the iubenda CMP both shows the reported notice AND consent-gates third-party content:⁠ the tribute YouTube iframe is served as `src="about:blank"` with `data-suppressedsrc`, class `_iub_cs_activate`, plus a first-party placeholder `div.home-film-privacy-placeholder` ("Accept the Privacy to watch the tribute"). The same gate is present in the unfiltered control and in the reporter's filtered baseline, i.e. it is the site's pre-consent state, not filtering damage. Neither linked document says whether a cookie-notice fix must also restore such gated embeds, whether the gate may be hidden, or whether granting the consent decision on the user's behalf (to make the embed load) is acceptable. The Cookie Notices policy only says non-essential cookies are declined by default "whenever possible" and that alternative methods are used when content depends on a cookie decision. The vision review here treats the pre-existing gate as part of the reported symptom and refused both a network block of the CMP loader and a cosmetic hide, so the run could not reach a verified rule.

Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — Reproduced both reporter-annotated overlays on www⁠.fritz-berger.de:⁠ a language-selection modal (.element_presence_switcher_modal, shown for non-German browser locales) and the consent banner #⁠cookiecontrol_notice_v2, whose data-visible="true" also generates a full-page whitish veil, while the modal leaves html.uk-modal-page locking page scroll. No single-rule candidate could clear all three parts (one spent attempt left the veil, one left the sticky banner, the ExtendedCSS variant applied only its first selector), so the two-rule fix is handed over unvalidated.

## Still visible after the rule

- Centered language-selection dialog over the Winter Deals hero at top of homepage — White centered modal with Berger logo and heading 'WELCOME TO THE BERGER CAMPING WEBSHOP!', English/German store buttons, 'You can change the language at any time in the webshop', and 'SELECT ANOTHER LANGUAGE ⁠>' link; it blocks the shop content behind it.
- Top-of-page shop area around the language modal and Winter Deals hero — Whitish dimming veil washes out the page behind the language modal, visibly reducing contrast across the header, navigation and hero area.
- Centered white dialog over the shop hero, roughly x=660–1260 and y=300–710 in the 1920×1080 overview — Language-selection modal with Berger logo, heading “WELCOME TO THE BERGER CAMPING WEBSHOP!”, explanatory text about www⁠.fritz-berger.de, English and German store buttons, and “SELECT ANOTHER LANGUAGE ⁠>” link.

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

## Missing information

- One-rule outcome cannot express this report's fix (needs hiding + scroll-lock release): The finish_fix contract allows exactly one filter rule per outcome, but the fritz-berger.de symptom needs two declaration targets:⁠ (a) hide the consent banner #⁠cookiecontrol_notice_v2, its generated veil html:⁠has(.cookiecontrol_notice_v2[⁠data-visible="true"]⁠):⁠:⁠before and the language modal .element_presence_switcher_modal, and (b) release the class-driven scroll lock `html.uk-modal-page { overflow: hidden }`. A single $#⁠@⁠#⁠ CSS rule carries one declaration block for its whole selector list, so display:⁠none (needed for the sticky banner and the veil) cannot be combined with overflow:⁠visible on html (display:⁠none on html blanks the page), and every apply_rule attempt failed on exactly that split (attempt 1 left the veil, attempt 2 left the sticky banner, attempt 3's ExtendedCSS comma list applied only its first selector). Guidance on whether a two-rule recommendation may be carried in one outcome, or which single rule the repository prefers, is missing.

<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"b31552c5e1d2524b7f58c07c5b5d074939b9e82a331793775745412defaa1ce3"} -->
The filter policy recommends closing without a rule

## Reproduced symptom

The reporter's "Промо" row on author.today is the site's own advertising:⁠ a sponsor-book carousel served by author.today's own placements API, own CDN images and /go/placement redirects, with no third-party ad host, and the site's own page /post/969899 ("Реклама на АТ") describes it as internal advertising. Filter policy forbids deliberately blocking the site's own (first-party) advertising, so no rule is proposed and the report is recommended for closing.

## Policy rationale

Run instruction (Filter policy):⁠ "The site's own advertising (first-party ads):⁠ no rule; recommend closing." AdGuard filter policy (KB, Limitations and exceptions):⁠ "The site’s own advertising should not be deliberately blocked. However, it should not be unblocked if the blocking is caused by general filtering rules." The reported block is served by the site itself:⁠ /api/v2/placements, /api/v2/placements/track, cm.author.today images and /go/placement click redirects, all thirdParty:⁠false in artifact:⁠har:⁠1bc46848-9325-4cc0-b2f9-4d96b152c2dd; no third-party ad host is present. The site labels and describes the block as its own advertising:⁠ the section header carries a "Промо" button whose "Что это?" popover opens /post/969899, titled "Реклама на АТ", which describes internal advertising for authors on the home page, in the catalogue and in the news feed. No other policy gate applies (no paywall, no anti-adblock wall, no scam or phishing content), so the first-party-advertising rule decides this report.

## Artifacts

issue.title: www.slorepo.com — anti-adblock modal (annoyance)
issue.body:
### URL
https://www.slorepo.com/

### Problem
On page load (~1 s after DOMContentLoaded) a full-screen anti-adblock modal appears: 「広告ブロックがオンになっています」 with a 「このまま見る（30）」 button that is disabled for 30 s (10 s on indexable pages), plus instructions to disable Private DNS / AdGuard. It re-appears on every page load.

The check is an inline `<script>` in `<head>`, no external file (the site says so in a comment: 「ブロッカーのリストに載りにくいよう、外部ファイルは使わず、部品の名前は毎回ランダム」), random element ids, inline styles — so there is nothing for a network rule to match:

1. off-screen bait node with `adsbox ad-banner ad-placement textads banner-ads pub_300x250`;
2. `fetch(HEAD, no-cors)` to `pagead2.googlesyndication.com/pagead/js/adsbygoogle.js` and `googleads.g.doubleclick.net/pagead/id`;
3. unreachable ⇒ probes its own `/robots.txt` to exclude a bad connection, then shows the modal;
4. if only the bait is hidden, it inspects `ins.adsbygoogle[data-ad-slot]` for a visible filled ad;
5. repeat visits (`localStorage.sr_ab`) get the modal immediately.

Reproduced by blocking the two ad hosts above (Base/Mobile Ads filter behaviour); the modal also appears with cosmetic filtering of the bait alone.

### Suggested rules
```
www.slorepo.com$$script[tag-content="__srabDone"]
www.slorepo.com##div[style*="z-index:2147483646"]
```
`$$` removes the offending inline script (HTML filtering). The second rule is a fallback for products/versions without HTML filtering — the overlay container always carries `z-index:2147483646` inline; verified the overlay is not re-created after hiding and the page stays usable.

### Filters
AdGuard Base filter + AdGuard Annoyances filter, AdGuard Browser Extension / AdGuard for Android on a mobile browser.

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — bananaball.com shows a fixed wpconsent cookie notice ("We use cookies…" with Preferences/Reject/Accept All) over the bottom of the mobile page even with AdGuard Cookie Notices enabled. The repo already hides this plugin's wrapper for another site, so the verified fix adds bananaball.com to that rule as bananaball.com#⁠#⁠#⁠wpconsent-container. ## Rule `bananaball.com###wpconsent-container` ## Policy rationale The report is a cookie-notice annoyance; per the run instruction's filter policy cookie notices belong to the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter, which may hide or block the corresponding scripts, and no closing rule applies (not the site's own advertising, not a paywall, not an anti-adblock wall). Maintainer rule 'Shared rules:⁠ extend them':⁠ the repository already hides this wpconsent wrapper with wpforms.com#⁠#⁠#⁠wpconsent-container, so the reported domain is added to that expression rather than a new rule line being written. Placement follows the repository layout and CONTRIBUTING:⁠ the Cookies section file that already keeps this rule, with the new domain added at the beginning of the cosmetic rule's domain list. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/a4d6e6b97324087978511e7a851f95deb96d2fa6/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Missing information - Reporter settings import cannot be applied on the adguard_cli (proxy) route: The issue carries an AdGuard for Android settings import URL, and the run instruction says a session launched with the reporter profile (reported_on_current + importUrl) is required to verify a rule. In the locked adguard_cli environment, launch_browser with extension:⁠"none" (the route's prescribed browser model) rejects any "settings" object, and the only launch that accepted the import (extension:⁠"prepared") returned settingsVerified:⁠false while starting a pinned browser-extension build that does not belong to the locked CLI route. It is therefore undocumented whether, and how, an Android settings import should be honoured for CLI-proxy validation, and the validation in this run had to run against the environment's own baseline instead of the reporter's filter selection. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — On news.jp the 「あなたにおすすめ」 block above the footer is an emptied Taboola widget:⁠ its slot is 0 px because the Taboola loader is blocked, leaving only the heading. The domain-scoped rule news.jp#⁠#⁠.recommend hides that leftover and was verified in the CLI proxy baseline (symptom resolved, page integrity intact, no residue). ## Rule `news.jp##.recommend` ## Policy rationale Run instruction policy:⁠ the site's own advertising, paywalls and German anti-adblock walls are the closed categories; this report is a leftover of a blocked third-party (Taboola) widget, so no policy rule closes it. Filter policy:⁠ the site's own advertising must not be deliberately blocked — the candidate hides only the emptied wrapper of a third-party ad widget that general rules (||taboola.com^$third-party, ||tblcontent.com^) already block; it neither blocks nor unblocks first-party content. No anti-adblock wall, paywall or dangerous-page category is involved, so the report is open to rule generation. ## Place in the list [JapaneseFilter/sections/specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/a4d6e6b97324087978511e7a851f95deb96d2fa6/JapaneseFilter/sections/specific.txt) By adding the domain to the existing rule on [line 8777](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/a4d6e6b97324087978511e7a851f95deb96d2fa6/JapaneseFilter/sections/specific.txt#L8777). ## Screenshots

Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — iza.ne.jp serves a first-party grey 「Google検索で iza を優先表示」 preferred-source self-promo banner above article headlines; the shared '.preferred-source' rule already covering eight sites (incl. sister site zakzak.co.jp) hides only the inner button on iza and left a blank gap, so the better fix is `iza.ne.jp##.preferred-source-wrapper`. That rule could not be validated because the filtering environment stopped providing phase proof (phase_proof_unavailable) after the first experiment, so it is carried unverified for human review.

## Candidate for review

`iza.ne.jp##.preferred-source-wrapper`

AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/subscriptions_specific.txt

Not verified: apply_rule could not run this candidate:⁠ after the first experiment the filtering environment reported the persistent limitation phase_proof_unavailable (stage:⁠ phase, 'The controlled browser observation did not complete'), and it repeated unchanged after a fresh browser session was launched, so no before/after phase proof exists for this rule. The related candidate that was run (adding iza.ne.jp to the shared '.preferred-source' rule at AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/subscriptions_specific.txt:⁠1157) hid the banner but was rejected by vision review:⁠ adLayoutResidue present, symptom not_resolved because the button-only selector leaves the wrapper's own 16px top/bottom margins as a blank gap above the headline (pageIntegrity intact, observedDamage empty). The carried rule hides the wrapper element that holds that margin box, which is why it is the better candidate, but it could not be visually confirmed.
